commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Orange / Brassy Tones
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Use ash (0/11) or blue (0/88) intensifier mixed with target shade. Choose ash family shades.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Yellow Brassy Tones
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Unwanted yellow warmth on lighter levels
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Use violet (0/66) or ash (0/11) intensifier. Choose violet or ash family shades.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Too Ashy / Green
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Result is overly ashy or has green cast
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Add warmth with gold (0/33) intensifier or switch to warm/golden family shades.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Resistant Gray Coverage
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Gray hair not covering evenly or fading quickly
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Use natural (N) family shades with 20-30 vol developer. Pre-soften if very resistant.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Going Dark to Light (4+ levels)
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Need to lift dark hair significantly lighter
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Use Special Blonde high-lift shades (12/0, 12/1, 12/7) with 40 vol. May need pre-lightening.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Dull / Faded Color
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Color lacks vibrancy and looks flat
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Add warm tones with gold (0/33) or mahogany (0/44 equivalent). Refresh with warm family.

commonCorrectionScenarios.name: Uneven Porosity / Color Grab
commonCorrectionScenarios.problem: Color absorbs unevenly, ends darker than roots
commonCorrectionScenarios.solution: Use lower developer on porous areas, fill color first. Choose neutral or warm shades.
commonCorrectionScenarios.developer: 10-20 vol on ends, 20-30 vol on roots
